purpose: Help HAL recognise affluent local nationals and HNWI clients whose insurance objective is comprehensive control, choice and continuity rather than merely basic access to healthcare.
recognition_signals: The client explicitly describes themselves as affluent, HNWI, high-net-worth, wealthy, executive, entrepreneur, business owner or family-office client.
The client says budget is secondary to quality, breadth or certainty of cover.
The client wants access to leading private hospitals or named international centres.
The client wants the option to seek planned treatment outside the country of residence.
The client wants private-room treatment, high annual limits, cancer/complex-care protection, broad outpatient cover or other comprehensive benefits under one contract.
The client splits time between countries, owns homes in multiple countries, travels frequently or expects future relocation.
The client values continuity of underwriting/cover if residence changes.
The client wants direct billing, international assistance, medical evacuation or cross-border case management.
The client wants a long-term comprehensive policy even though they are a local national rather than an expatriate.

core_value_dimensions.title: Choice of provider and treatment location
core_value_dimensions.argument: For an affluent/HNWI client, the issue may be the freedom to choose private hospitals, specialists or treatment locations rather than reliance on a single domestic network.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Do not claim every IPMI policy permits unrestricted provider choice; verify the specific policy/network and pre-authorisation rules.

core_value_dimensions.title: Cross-border planned treatment
core_value_dimensions.argument: An HNWI client may value the option to obtain eligible planned treatment in another country, including the home country or an international centre of excellence.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Actual geographical cover and planned-treatment rules must be verified from the selected policy.

core_value_dimensions.title: Long-term continuity and portability
core_value_dimensions.argument: For clients whose residence or lifestyle may change, a portable international policy may reduce the need to replace a domestic policy solely because they move.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Portability is not automatic in every destination. Eligibility, pricing and regulation can change after relocation.

core_value_dimensions.title: High financial ceilings for complex care
core_value_dimensions.argument: HNWI clients often seek high annual limits and fewer restrictive benefit sublimits so that a serious cancer, transplant or complex admission is not constrained by a modest domestic sublimit.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Do not assume a local plan has low limits. Compare the actual local and international contracts.

core_value_dimensions.title: International service infrastructure
core_value_dimensions.argument: Direct billing, international assistance, multilingual claims support and medical case coordination may be important to clients who value convenience and reduced administrative friction.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Service levels vary by insurer, country, provider and claim type.

core_value_dimensions.title: Comprehensive protection under one contract
core_value_dimensions.argument: Some HNWI clients prefer one contract combining inpatient, outpatient, diagnostics, mental health, dental, optical, maternity or wellness benefits rather than assembling fragmented domestic solutions.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Not every IPMI plan contains every benefit; modules, waiting periods and limits must be verified.

core_value_dimensions.title: Local nationals can have an IPMI need
core_value_dimensions.argument: International health insurance can be relevant to an affluent local national even with no expatriate status when their objective is international provider choice, broader geographic treatment options or long-term comprehensive protection.
core_value_dimensions.caveat: Carrier eligibility for local nationals must be checked. Some products are designed primarily for expatriates or require prior approval for local nationals.

what_not_to_say: Do not say a local plan can never be comprehensive.
Do not say a wealthy client 'needs' IPMI merely because they are wealthy.
Do not imply that the public system is unsafe or clinically inferior.
Do not use out-of-pocket statistics as proof that insured people were denied claims.
Do not infer that people paying out of pocket were uninsured.
Do not promise access to any named hospital without checking network/direct-billing rules.
Do not equate high annual limits with unlimited cover.
suggested_discovery_questions: If you needed major treatment, would you want the option to choose a hospital outside your country of residence?
Is keeping the same long-term cover if you move country important to you?
Do you want unrestricted or broad private-hospital choice to be a priority?
Would you prefer a comprehensive plan including outpatient and additional benefits, or mainly catastrophic inpatient protection?
Is your priority lowest premium, or maximum breadth and flexibility of cover?
Would direct settlement with major hospitals and international assistance be valuable to you?
